verses.text: A troublemaker named Sheba son of Bichri, from the tribe of Benjamin, was there. He blew the trumpet and shouted, “We have no share in David and no inheritance in Jesse's son. Back to your tents, Israel!”
All the men of Israel stopped following David and followed Sheba son of Bichri. The men of Judah stayed with their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

When David came home to Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he'd left to look after the palace and put them under guard. He provided for them and never slept with them again. They lived in confinement as widows until they died.
The king told Amasa, “Call the men of Judah together for me within three days, and be back here yourself.”
So Amasa went to call up the men of Judah, but he took longer than the king had allowed.
David told Abishai, “Sheba son of Bichri is going to do us more harm than Absalom did. Take my men and go after him before he reaches fortified towns and gets away from us.”
Joab's men went with him, along with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and the best fighters. They left Jerusalem to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.
At the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab was in his battle clothes, with a sword strapped at his waist in its sheath. As he stepped forward, the sword slipped out.
Joab said, “How are you, my brother?” With his right hand he took Amasa by the beard to greet him with a kiss.

Amasa paid no attention to the sword in Joab's hand. Joab struck him in the belly, spilling his intestines onto the ground. Amasa died from that one blow. Joab and his brother Abishai went after Sheba son of Bichri.
One of Joab's young men stood by Amasa and called, “Whoever supports Joab and stands with David, follow Joab!”
Amasa lay in his blood in the middle of the road. The man saw that everyone who came by stopped, so he dragged Amasa off the road into a field and threw a garment over him.
Once Amasa was off the road, everyone followed Joab in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.
Sheba went through all the tribes of Israel to Abel in Beth Maacah. All the Berites came together and followed him there.
Joab's forces reached Abel of Beth Maacah and laid siege to Sheba there. They heaped up a siege ramp against the city's defenses and battering parties began trying to bring down the wall.
A wise woman called out from the city, “Listen! Listen! Tell Joab to come close. I need to speak to him.”
Joab came closer. “Are you Joab?” she asked. “I am,” he answered. She said, “Please listen to what I have to say.” He replied, “I'm listening.”
She told him, “In the old days people used to say, ‘Ask for advice at Abel,’ and that would settle the matter.
I'm one of Israel's peaceful and faithful people. You're trying to destroy a city that's like a mother in Israel. Why swallow up what belongs to the LORD?”
Joab answered, “I'd never dream of swallowing it up or destroying it.

Here's what's going on. A man from the hill country of Ephraim named Sheba son of Bichri has risen up against King David. Hand over that one man and I'll leave the city.” The woman answered, “His head will be thrown to you over the wall.”

The woman went to all the people with her wise advice. They cut off Sheba son of Bichri's head and threw it to Joab. He blew the trumpet, and his men withdrew from the city and went to their own tents. Joab went back to the king in Jerusalem.
Joab commanded Israel's whole army, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada commanded the Cherethites and Pelethites.
Adoram was in charge of forced labor, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the official records.
Sheva was the scribe, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
Ira the Jairite was David's chief minister.
